highlights.title: Webb: VAR had 'tunnel vision' on Haaland which led to Enzo error
highlights.summary: Pro Ref chief Howard Webb says VAR missed Enzo Fernandez being offside for Erling Haaland's winning goal in the Manchester derby due to "tunnel vision".
body: Webb says he is "really disappointed" by the decision to award the goal, which was initially ruled out on the field due to Haaland being flagged offside.
VAR then checked the incident and determined the striker was onside but failed to account for Enzo Fernandez impacting play from an offside position.

Fernandez dived for the ball before it was steered home by Haaland, and despite severely hindering Lisandro Martinez and Senne Lammens, Fernandez's offside position was overlooked once the VAR officials had confirmed he had not touched the ball - even though a player can be offside without touching the ball.
Webb told Mic'd Up: "The on-field decision was not against Fernandez; it was against Haaland. When the VAR starts their check, they see that Haaland is actually onside by three centimetres.

highlights.title: Target Will Be Unusually Strict For Pokémon's 30th Anniversary TCG Set Release
highlights.summary: You can buy Pokémon cards nearly anywhere these days, but most people in the United States default to buying TCG products at Target stores. Target, it seems, is taking that association seriously for the impending launch of the Pokémon 30th Anniversary set.
body: Target customers may already have noticed this change. Throughout September, many Target locations have set up elaborate Pokémon product displays near the electronics section in the back of the store. According to leaked documentation, these shelves won't be limited to 30th Anniversary items — fans should also expect to see recent products, like the new Target-exclusive Pokémon Owala bottles.

The retailer is apparently increasing its security measures around the release as well. The exact rules will vary by location, and fans who plan on lining up early might do well to check with their local store. However, as first reported by Pokémon restock influencer BritBrattv, Pokémon fans should expect a stricter sales system for the 30th Anniversary products. Many stores will make use of added security personnel to manage potentially long and unruly lines, and to direct parking lot traffic.

He added that the “efforts to make sure that we have free and fair elections are not going to stop just in November or after or thereafter”.
The attorney general went on to defend the president’s earlier criticism of the justices on the bench who ruled to block his order.

“He [Trump] is very frustrated,” Blanche said. “He has every right, and indeed he should communicate his concerns with the supreme court whenever he has them. highlights.title: Zack Snyder Says 300 Is the ‘Gayest Movie Ever Made,' Defends The Last Photograph Amid Online Backlash
highlights.summary: Zach Snyder is going viral off the heels of his latest movie, The Last Photograph, as well as his subsequent interview with Variety where he responded to the backlash against the film and made a few eyebrow-raising remarks about his previous work.
body: Reviews for Snyder’s The Last Photograph have been brutal. A swath of scathing opinions hit the net after its screening at the Toronto International Film Festival over the weekend, where Snyder joked that the audience in attendance might be the only ones to ever see it on the silver screen — and based on critical reception to the project, that might be a legitimate possibility.

For example, IGN gave the bloody action flick a 4 out of ten, calling it a “trudging revenge saga that points to self-critique” that’s “filled with big ideas that go nowhere.” Discourse online, however, has been far more vitriolic. According to Snyder himself, users on social media have been labeling him a “fascist” and a “homophobe” in the wake of these scalding reviews.

“Look, I’m famously surrounded by a particular discourse that happens around my movies. It’s incredibly charged. And I thought, for the smallest of moments, that because it’s a small movie and it’s really not that big of a deal, that it’d be allowed to exist on whatever level it is. What kind of noise does a tiny movie like this warrant from the world?” he said in a September 15 interview with Variety.

highlights.title: There are two kinds of people in this world: hosts or guests. Nobody can be both | Polly Hudson
highlights.summary: My hosting persona is an edgier version of Manuel from Fawlty Towers. Invite me to yours, however, and I am a nonstop delight. My epiphany came between the starter and the main.
body: The problem now is payback. Post epiphany, I only want to be the guest star and never host again. But is it OK for all of us to stay in our lanes, play only to our strengths? Obviously, that’s the logical solution, which would be better and more enjoyable for everybody. But if one party repeatedly doles out invites while the other accepts but never returns the favour, will it lead to resentment? I suppose only the hosts among us can answer that. Which is worse? Feeling like you’re being taken advantage of? Or having to come to my house for dinner?

highlights.title: 18-year-old dies of measles in PA from severe neurological complication
highlights.summary: A fourth person in Pennsylvania has died of measles, the state health department confirmed Tuesday. The latest death was in an unvaccinated 18-year-old resident of Mifflin County.
body: In the announcement, the state health department also confirmed a county coroner’s report over the weekend of the death of an unvaccinated 40-year-old woman in Jefferson County. The state had previously reported two deaths in Lancaster County, both were in infants— a newborn boy and a 6-week-old girl, both too young to be vaccinated.

According to the Mifflin County coroner, Andrea L. Alcalde, the 18-year-old’s cause of death was determined to be acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM), which is a rare but known severe complication of measles. The condition is characterized by a rapidly progressing autoimmune disorder in which aberrant inflammation from an infection strips away the protective coverings of nerve cells in the brain and spinal cord. Before measles vaccines were widely used, ADEM was commonly associated with measles, though other viral infections can also spur its development.

In a new release posted to the coroner’s Facebook page Tuesday, Alcalde said the death determination was made after a review of medical records and all available information. Alcalde said no other information would be released about the deceased.

At the top of the table, Ethan Bamber and Sam Hain ensured Warwickshire maintained their title challenge by ending the first day against Essex with a 17-run lead with one wicket in hand.

In the end, a gruesome serial killer’s spree, alongside the personal and collective upheaval their presence has wrought, touches Bret (Igby Rigney) and his inner circle in a new, unsettling way with the murder of producer Terry Schaffer (Wes Bentley). The whodunnit cliffhanger, which posits that just about any one of the characters could be the culprit, is the result of a splintering not only from Ellis’ text, but of the friendships and even psyches among this glossy gaggle of ‘80s high school elites.

In the episode’s final moments, set to The Go-Go’s “Our Lips Are Sealed,” the camera pans across a holding room, everyone striking a pose as they await police questioning. highlights.title: Go with the flow: do you need to filter US tap water?
highlights.summary: Experts share best practices for considering water filters – whether you’re drinking municipally treated water or relying on a well. Americans have a lot of questions about their drinking water. How is it treated? What’s in it? Most importantly, is it safe?
body: “I’ve even been out to eat where people overhear me talking about my work and come over to ask me a question about their tap water,” said Kimberly Parker, an environmental engineer who studies chemical contaminants in drinking water at Washington University in St Louis.

Most Americans have access to municipal water, which “tends to be really well treated” and largely safe to drink, said Parker. Across the US, water is monitored for contamination via centralized infrastructure at federal and state levels.
In Parker’s experience, “many environmental engineers choose not to use filtered water” because of their informed confidence in the safety of tap water, she said.
Nevertheless, whether you’re drinking municipally treated water or relying on a well, there are water-safety challenges.

highlights.title: SpaceX declares Starship ready for orbit, sets launch date next week
highlights.summary: Pending regulatory approval, SpaceX said today it intends to launch its 14th Starship mission as early as September 22. This flight is notable, as it will be the first time that SpaceX attempts to launch the experimental vehicle into orbit.
body: The company set a target liftoff time of 7:15 am local in Texas (12:15 UTC), with a 75-minute launch window. Sunrise in Brownsville, Texas, is 7:17 am CT, so the launch could make for some striking imagery.

The super heavy lift rocket will be carrying 26 of the larger V3 Starlink satellites into an orbit 275 km above the Earth. In an update on its website, SpaceX said the Starship upper stage will seek to complete six orbits around the Earth before completing its mission after about 10 hours.

Reaching orbit would mark a significant milestone in the company’s Starship development campaign, which conducted its first test flight on April 20, 2023, and has since made progress in fits and starts. With the upcoming mission, SpaceX continues to make modifications to the Starship vehicle as it seeks to improve the third iteration of the Super Heavy booster and Starship upper stage. After recent successes, the company appears to be closer to developing a fully reusable, super heavy lift rocket.

highlights.title: The Last Of Us Season 3 Is Probably The Final Season, HBO Says Yet Again
highlights.summary: HBO boss Casey Bloys has once again said that the upcoming third season of The Last of Us is expected to be its last. He told Deadline that Season 3 is coming in 2027, though did not confirm when in the year.
body: In January this year, Bloys was asked if Season 3 is going to be the last, and he said, "It certainly seems that way." However, at the time, Bloys admitted that a decision like that would come down to Mazin.
Before this, Mazin said that Season 4 was essential to bring the show to a conclusion. However, Bloys has indicated that the show may wrap up its run with Season 3, which could be a longer season.
“Craig is still working it out whether it will be two more seasons or one more long season. It hasn’t been decided yet, and I’m following Craig’s lead on that,” Bloys said in 2025.

In a big shift for the series, franchise creator Naughty Dog is not involved creatively in Season 3, and Neil Druckmann dropped out as a writer/director. One of the companies currently carrying the torch for minivans is Kia, which has sold its popular Carnival minivan here since 2021. Kia is also one of the few automakers making all-electric vans. This week, the Korean automaker rolled out its new PV7 at IAA Transportation in Germany. highlights.title: The AI graveyard: a running list of projects and startups that didn’t make it
highlights.summary: From Apple's repeatedly delayed Siri AI to OpenAI's messy 'super app' launch, here's a look at the AI projects that shut down or missed expectations.
body: Relay, an AI-powered workflow automation tool built as an alternative to Zapier, shut down entirely on Monday. The product let users automate email and task workflows using AI agents, but as OpenAI, Google, and other larger platforms built similar automation directly into their own tools, five-year-old Relay struggled to hold on to a reason to exist as a stand-alone product.

Relay — a startup outpaced by bigger platforms — is one version of the story playing out right now. But plenty of AI bets never even survive inside the companies that build them. According to S&P Global Market Intelligence, about 42% of AI initiatives are ultimately abandoned by their corporate parents. The reasons vary: insufficient funding, technical challenges, competition, difficulty scaling, or just weak user demand.

The result is a growing AI graveyard. Below is a look at some of the most notable AI products, startups, launches, and bets that have shut down, pivoted, or significantly missed expectations. Think of it less as a scorecard of flops than as a record of what these attempts can (hopefully) teach the rest of the industry.

The event will begin on Sept. 22 and run through Oct. 13. The main event of the crossover will be the Wildcard game mode that turns the battle royale into an all-out brawl. Rather than shoot at each other, players will pick from four Street Fighter characters and use melee attacks to take down enemies. Collecting coins will fill a Fighter Gauge that lets you enter Fighter Form, which unlocks more special abilities.

The mode will take place on a remixed version of the Olympus map, full of nods to Capcom's series. The final round will be called Showdown and will grant the remaining players an infinite Fight Gauge so that everyone can end the game on an explosive note.

Each skin costs 2,150 Apex Coins. In addition to the character skins, there will be eight weapon skins, two skydive emotes, holosprays, stickers, badges, trackers, and frames. Players will earn Zenny in every match, which can be used to unlock items. One such item will be an Epic skin for Lifeline that makes her look like Street Fighter's Li-Fen.

body: When Agility’s new Digit 5 robot detects a person at a distance, it can autonomously take precautions, like moving to avoid the person or standing still so the person can pass by without getting closer. If a person is getting into close proximity with Digit 5, the robot can even choose to squat and assume a seated position.

highlights.title: US data centers could consume more natural gas than Germany and Japan combined by 2035
highlights.summary: The AI frenzy could push U.S. data centers to become one of the largest consumers of natural gas in the world.
body: The AI race has grown so frenzied that, by 2035, U.S. data centers are projected to consume more natural gas than Germany and Japan combined.

Over the next decade, data centers are expected to be the second-strongest driver of natural gas demand growth after LNG exports. The facilities could consume about 18 billion cubic feet per day, according to a new report from BloombergNEF, nearly double the amount the organization predicted just nine months ago.
The new forecast takes into account that not all announced data center projects will be completed.

Data centers that produce power onsite have grabbed headlines in recent months, with Meta, Microsoft, Google, and Amazon all announcing plans for new natural gas power plants that will bypass the grid. Projects such as these will consume 2.9 billion to 3.4 billion cubic feet per day by 2035. That’s about as much as all data centers consume today, including natural gas used to generate power for the grid.
points: The AI frenzy could push U.S. data centers to become one of the largest consumers of natural gas in the world.
